definition: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) is the combination of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies with the Internet of things (IoT) infrastructure to create systems capable of sensing, learning, and acting on data without continuous human intervention.
details: While IoT focuses on connectivity and sensor data collection, AI enables IoT devices to analyse data in real time and produce actionable outputs, including automated decisions at the edge.

explainer.lead: Artificial Intelligence of Things, or AIoT, adds artificial intelligence to connected sensor-based systems so they can interpret data and act on it. This matters because devices can respond in real time instead of merely collecting information or waiting for continuous human direction.

tiers.eli5: Regular connected gadgets just collect readings and send them along, like a smoke alarm that only beeps. AIoT is more like a smoke alarm that also works out whether it's a real fire and calls for help on its own.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pair IoT sensor pipelines with AI models, often running inference at the edge so decisions happen in real time. A common pitfall is assuming IoT's connectivity alone gives you this; the AI layer has to be designed in to turn data into automated actions.
tiers.paperLevel: AIoT is defined as AI technologies combined with IoT infrastructure to form systems that sense, learn and act on data without continuous human intervention. The scope described is qualitative; no specific architecture or performance guarantee is given.

explainer.example: Consider a connected room-temperature sensor. It reports a falling temperature, an AI component analyses the reading immediately and decides that heating is needed, and the system turns on the heater without someone first reviewing the sensor data.
explainer.intuition: An IoT system gives devices senses and connections; AIoT adds the ability to interpret what they sense and choose an action. The result is a loop from observation to analysis to action, rather than a stream of readings for people to handle.
howItWorks: IoT sensors collect data about the environment or equipment.
The IoT infrastructure connects the devices and carries their data.
AI analyses the data in real time and learns patterns relevant to the task.
The analysis produces an actionable output or automated decision, potentially at the edge.
The system acts on that output without requiring continuous human intervention.
explainer.whyItMatters: AIoT turns connected sensing into timely action. Real-time analysis and edge decisions can reduce the need for people to continuously monitor readings and manually operate each device.
misconceptions: A connected sensor network is not automatically AIoT; it also needs AI-based analysis that produces actionable outputs.
AIoT is not limited to sending data elsewhere for processing, because automated decisions can happen at the edge.
